title: What to eat
intro: Two group-size decisions drove this list: several well-regarded local soba shops turned out to have private rooms too small for 8 (Inokoya Yamagatada's curtain-divided rooms seat only 4-6), so they're noted as casual/overflow options rather than the flagship picks. Taimenseki, Izu no Hana, and Sakaeya Honten are informal single-visit picks, not group-booked meals.

items.name: Yonezawa Beef Tokiwa
items.address: 2-9 Sachimachi, Yamagata (ground floor, Daiwa Roynet Hotel Yamagata Ekimae)
items.why: Private room seats up to 14 — the trip's one confirmed group-size fit for a splurge dinner. Also bookable online via TableCheck.

items.name: Soba Sanbyakubou
items.how: Inside the Beninokura complex, ≈10 min walk from Yamagata Station
items.why: The private storehouse room (蔵座敷) seats up to 30, comfortably fitting the group — pairs naturally with the Beninokura warehouse visit next door.

items.name: Takifudo Namasoba
items.how: Short walk from Yamadera Station, near the mountain entrance
items.why: ≈50 seats plus a 2nd-floor tatami room for 50+ — the best-corroborated capacity fit for a group of 8 near Yamadera, and known for group/tour-bus dining.
items.crowd_tip: Call ahead in koyo (foliage) season — this is a well-known tour-group stop and walk-in risk is real once the leaves turn.

items.name: Inokoya Yamagatada
items.why: Imoni (taro stew) served year-round in individual mini-hearth pots — thematically ideal, but private rooms seat only 4-6 (curtain-divided). Good for a casual/overflow meal, not the flagship group dinner.

items.name: Taimenseki
items.how: At the foot of the mountain, right by Yamadera Station — window seats over the Senzan Line tracks and the Tachiya River
items.why: A quick soba rest-stop for imoni-soba or itasoba on the way to or from the climb — no group-booking policy is posted, so treat it as an informal option rather than a reserved group meal.

items.name: Izu no Hana
items.hours: 11:00-18:00 (soba last order 17:30); a reservation-only evening menu runs 17:00-19:00
items.how: On Ginzan Onsen's main street, an easy walk from Ginzanso
items.why: A soba-and-dessert stop inside the onsen village itself — call ahead for a table of 8, since the shop takes domestic group bookings only when its own capacity allows and does not accept overseas tour-operator bookings.

items.name: Sakaeya Honten
items.how: In Honcho, central Yamagata city — exact walking distance from the station isn't confirmed
items.why: Self-declared birthplace of hiyashi ramen (chilled ramen), invented here in 1952 — a genuinely local claim the city's own heritage page confirms only in outline, without naming a shop. Hours aren't posted; call ahead.
